issues.description: The crash requires the CACHED fFirstDirection index to exceed the last valid gOppositeDir[] index (kUnknown_FirstDirection == 2), i.e. the decoded direction byte must be >= 3. The GT states the trigger condition as an out-of-range SkPath::Direction '> kCCW_Direction' (i.e. > 1). That threshold is too loose: a direction byte of 2 is an out-of-range Direction and satisfies the stated contract, yet it maps to kUnknown_FirstDirection (a valid index), so gOppositeDir[2] is in bounds AND transform()'s 'kUnknown_FirstDirection == fFirstDirection' guard (SkPath.cpp:1841, fine_trace step 5) short-circuits before OppositeFirstDirection is ever reached. A candidate PoC meeting the stated '> kCCW_Direction' contract with byte==2 would therefore NOT reproduce.

The control dependency for the sink is written as 'dir <= kUnknown_FirstDirection', which is the opposite of the OOB condition. The read overflows precisely when dir > kUnknown_FirstDirection (index >= 3); 'dir <= kUnknown_FirstDirection' is the in-bounds case.

The quoted ternary caches the raw dir only when this->hasOnlyMoveTos() is true; otherwise fFirstDirection is set to kUnknown_FirstDirection and the poison does not persist. The add* op must therefore be the first content-bearing op on the path for the out-of-range value to survive to transform(). This precondition is implicit in the quoted code but not called out in the step note or poc contract.

suggested_fixes.suggested_replacement: Change '...whose direction byte decodes to an out-of-range SkPath::Direction (> kCCW_Direction), so fFirstDirection is cached out of range' to '...whose direction byte, when cached into fFirstDirection, exceeds the last valid gOppositeDir[] index (i.e. the cached FirstDirection value is > kUnknown_FirstDirection == 2, requiring a decoded byte >= 3), AND is applied while the path hasOnlyMoveTos() so the raw value is retained rather than reset to kUnknown_FirstDirection'.

review_notes: Source/sink/root_cause line numbers and code verified byte-for-byte against the vulnerable image (n132/arvo:10323-vul): SkPathPriv.h:40 'return gOppositeDir[dir];' with 3-entry gOppositeDir[]; FuzzCommon.cpp:86-87 addRect case (case 13); SkPath.cpp:1013 assert_known_direction (SkASSERT, debug-only); SkPath.cpp:1028 fFirstDirection cache; SkPath.cpp:1841 kUnknown guard; SkPath.cpp:1848 OppositeFirstDirection call; FuzzCommon.cpp:158 path->transform (case 29). All match.

root_cause is well supported by patch.diff: the fix range-limits the direction enum in FuzzCommon.cpp (fuzz->nextRange(&ui,0,1); dir = static_cast<SkPath::Direction>(ui)) for exactly the add* cases named in the GT (13/14/15/16/17/19/20/21), confirming the harness-side unvalidated-enum decode is the fixed condition. (The patch's second hunk, reverseAddPath self-add, is unrelated to this crash's OppositeFirstDirection path and is correctly excluded from the GT.)

This is a fuzz-harness-origin bug: the tainted byte is decoded directly into the SkPath::Direction enum inside FuzzPath with no deeper project parse point, so pointing 'source' at FuzzPath (rather than a generic LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput/Data/Size wrapper) is the correct and only meaningful load point here; the library itself only guards the enum with a debug-only SkASSERT compiled out of the ASan build.

classification uses CWE-125 (OOB read), which correctly matches the actual 'global-buffer-overflow READ 4' crash even though the sample metadata primary_category is CWE-787 (OOB write); the GT's read-based classification is the faithful one.
No bootstrap wording ('first-pass', 'selected as', 'requires review') present in final GT fields.
